title: Operational Risk Management and Sustainable Energy Production Efficiency in Eritrea: The Mediating Roles of Production Technology Risk and Early Warning Management Effectiveness
content: Improving sustainable energy production efficiency is a priority for resource-constrained countries, where environmental stress, equipment degradation, managerial weaknesses and human operational errors can threaten reliable energy supply. This study develops and tests an integrated operational risk model for sustainable energy production in Eritrea. Drawing on the Resource-Based View and Multi-Hazard Early Warning Systems perspective, it examines whether human, environmental, management and equipment risks affect sustainable energy production efficiency through production technology risk and early warning management effectiveness. Survey data were collected from 300 respondents with direct knowledge of production, maintenance, safety, monitoring and warning-response activities in sustainable energy production industries. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modelling and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis. The results show that all four risk dimensions significantly increase production technology risk, with human risk exerting the strongest effect. Production technology risk is positively associated with early warning management effectiveness, which is the strongest direct predictor of sustainable energy production efficiency. The mediation results confirm that production technology risk and early warning management effectiveness transmit the effects of operational risks to efficiency outcomes, while the configurational analysis reveals multiple alternative pathways to high efficiency. The findings suggest that sustainable energy performance depends not only on technical assets but also on coordinated risk knowledge, monitoring, maintenance and rapid-response capabilities.
